focus.jnote: Everything today hinges on one 8:30 release. The long-delayed September jobs report prints this morning, with the Dow Jones consensus near +84K payrolls and unemployment ~4.1%. It lands into a tape where the 10-year yield sits near ~5.24% (30Y ~5.60%), just off multi-decade highs hit Thursday. Oil is a second live wire — WTI jumped back above ~$92 (Brent above $100) after Chinese refiners suspended most October fuel exports, deepening a global diesel crunch. Futures are modestly higher ahead of the number, and the VIX is roughly flat near ~16.4. This is a data-and-headline tape, not one a Sniper sells premium into — and the scanner confirmed it: zero names cleared the criteria today.
focus.notdown: Energy (XLE, XOM, CVX, OXY) is the day’s clearest bid as China’s fuel-export halt tightens an already strained global market — XLE led Thursday with energy up nearly 2%. But this is a two-sided supply-shock trade, not a clean Sniper: one de-escalation or export-normalization headline and crude gives back the spike. And with the jobs report in minutes, even energy gaps with the index. Watch-only, not a table-pounder.
focus.notup: Rate-sensitive groups (REITs, utilities, small caps, housing) stay pressured with the 10Y near ~5.24% and oil feeding inflation fear. But selling bear calls into the jobs print carries violent squeeze risk on any soft-labor headline (good-news-is-bad-news works both ways here) — the disciplined answer is to sell nothing new today.

Decisively, the September jobs report inside the next hour is a market-moving release that cannot be GREEN under the rules, stacked on a bond market at ~5.24% multi-decade-high yields and a fresh oil supply shock. risks: September jobs report · Fri 10/2, 8:30 ET — the long-delayed payrolls print (consensus ~84–90K, unemployment ~4.1%) lands into a rate-pressured tape and sets up the Oct 28 FOMC. Both a hot and a too-soft number carry gap risk into the weekend. This is the number-one thing to watch.

Bond yields — 10Y near ~5.24%, 30Y ~5.60%, both near multi-decade highs — the 10Y touched ~5.34% intraday Thursday, its highest since 2002, before easing. A hot jobs number could send yields back up and hit rate-sensitive growth, REITs, utilities and small caps hardest.

Oil & the diesel crunch — China suspended most October fuel exports, pushing WTI back above ~$92 and Brent above $100 into an already-tight global diesel market. A further spike feeds inflation fear and compounds the yield pressure.
US–Iran war & Ukraine refinery strikes — the unresolved conflict backdrop and ongoing attacks on Russian refineries keep a supply-disruption premium in energy; any escalation sends crude vertical.
Q3 earnings & midterms ahead — earnings season starts in a few weeks and the November midterms loom; single-stock and event risk is building just as the macro tape stays on edge.
Fed October decision (Oct 28) — markets price ~21–28% odds of a hike; this jobs report is the swing input, so the labor read reverberates through rates for weeks.
